Package com.egradx.auth.profile

Class EgradxProfileService

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.profile.EgradxProfileService
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware
public class EgradxProfileService extends Object implements org.springframework.context.ApplicationEventPublisherAware
User profiles: personal details, contact addresses per channel, and communication preferences.

An in-process API with no access control of its own, like the other egradx-auth services. The REST controllers decide who may call what — a person on their own profile, or an administrator of an organization the person belongs to.

Every method that shows or changes contacts or preferences takes the organization being acted in. What applies everywhere is visible from any organization; what is scoped to one organization is visible only from that one. So an administrator of one organization never sees a Slack id someone keeps for another.

Only a verified address is ever returned for sending (resolveAddress(java.util.UUID, java.util.UUID, java.lang.String)). An address becomes verified by the person confirming a code sent to it, or by an administrator vouching for it; changing it makes it unverified again.

      Sends a fresh code to the address, replacing any earlier one.

      ValidationException - with CONTACT_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE if nothing can send it, CONTACT_VERIFICATION_RATE_LIMITED if asked again too soon, or CONTACT_ALREADY_VERIFIED

    • confirmVerification

      @Transactional(noRollbackFor=ValidationException.class) public EgradxContactDto confirmVerification(UUID userId, UUID organizationId, UUID contactId, String code)
      Checks a code. A wrong one counts against the limit, and that count is kept even though an exception is thrown — which is what noRollbackFor is for; otherwise every wrong guess would be rolled back and the limit could never be reached.
